To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the success of capacity-building depends on the following factors: a. the Terms of Reference, which need to be drafted in a bottom-up and demand-driven fashion, and b. the level of the target group.

capacity building in urban lending is more successful when: (1) the Terms of Reference are drafted in a bottom-up and demand-driven fashion, (2) capacity building activities are tailored to the ability (and willingness) of the towns to change, (3) capacity building at local level is reciprocated by state governments and (4) TA activities are more strongly integrated in loan component activities and are sustained throughout the project period.

the most important factor for the success of capacity development is the commitment to the programme of all stakeholders.
capacity building should be a continuous process, and not an isolated event.

The main takeaway from our work is that
capacity building should not be considered as an isolated activity, but as part of the overall project cycle, which includes the preparation and implementation of the urban project.
TA should not be seen as a separate component of a project, but as part of the project itself.
